chunks: From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abu Jameela, from Lays Al-Murady, who said:

Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) clothed Usamah ibn Zayd with a silk garment (hullah), so he went out wearing it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Wait, O Usamah! Indeed, it is worn by the one who has no manners (khalaq) for him, so distribute it among your women.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on men wearing silk according to this hadith from Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) observes Usamah ibn Zayd wearing a silk garment (*hulla*) and cautions him, stating that silk is reserved for those who lack *khalaq* (moral character or distinction), implying it is a marker of luxury for the less virtuous. He then instructs Usamah to distribute the garment among the women, reflecting the Shia scholarly view that silk is permissible for women but generally discouraged or prohibited for men as a sign of modesty and distinction from the extravagant. This incident highlights the nuanced approach to material luxury in Islamic tradition, where the same item carries different spiritual and social weights depending on the wearer's gender and character.

en.hubeali: From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abu Jameela, from Lays Al Murady who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said that Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> clothed Asama Bin Zayd with a silk garment (for a military expedition). Then (after the battle) he came out wearing it, so he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘No, O Asama! But rather it is worn by the one who has no manners for him, therefore distribute it between your womenfolk’.
en.sarwar: 2. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from ibn Faddal from abu Jamilah from Layth al-Muradiy who has said the following: “

Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, made ‘Usamah ibn Zayd dress in silk (during a war). He (after the war) came out in public in that dress. He (the Messenger of Allah), said, ‘O ‘Usamah, wait. Those who wear this (silk) do not have a share (in morality) so you must divide it among your women.’”
